title: Preservation of simulator safety
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, and let $x$ be an input word over the folded alphabet. If a configuration $c$ of the folding simulator of $M$ on $x$ satisfies the safety invariant—its state is not the fresh initial state, all work-head positions are nonnegative, and each nonnegative work-tape cell has its origin flag set exactly at position $0$—then the configuration after one simulator step also satisfies the safety invariant.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$x$ is a word over the folded alphabet
$c$ is a configuration of the folding simulator on $x$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape machine over a finite alphabet with decidable equality and
let $c$ be a configuration of the folding simulator of $M$, on an arbitrary
folded-alphabet input, satisfying the safety invariant.  Then the configuration
obtained after one step of the simulator also satisfies the safety invariant.
